issues.title: --help agent omits --clear, --limit, --offset flags for agent list

sections.body: Run `./b4w.ps1 --help agent` and observe that `agent list` is listed with no flags.
sections.label: Reproduction

sections.body: The --help agent output should mention key flags like --clear, --limit, --offset for agent list, similar to how other commands surface their options.
sections.label: Expected Behavior

sections.body: `--help agent` shows: `agent list — List all tracked agent tasks and their status` with no flag hints. Users must run `agent list --help` (two levels deep) to discover --clear.
sections.label: Actual Behavior

sections.body: The category-level help filter (`--help agent`) only renders subcommand names and one-line descriptions. It does not enumerate per-subcommand flags. The implementation likely iterates over subcommands and prints their `about` strings without including their argument/flag definitions.
sections.label: Root Cause Analysis

sections.body: cli/browser4-cli/src/ — likely in the help rendering or clap configuration where category filters are applied
sections.label: Code Pointer

sections.body:
- Extend `--help agent` to show a brief flags summary per subcommand (e.g., `agent list [--clear] [--limit N] [--offset N]`)
- Alternatively, add a hint at the bottom: "Run `agent list --help` for detailed options."
sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement

issues.title: Pre-existing tasks from prior sessions visible on first agent list

sections.body: Run `agent list` as a new user. If any prior CLI session submitted agent tasks, they appear in the list.
sections.label: Reproduction

sections.body: A new user's first `agent list` should either show no tasks or clearly distinguish between the current session's tasks and tasks from prior sessions.
sections.label: Expected Behavior

sections.body: When I ran `agent list`, 3 tasks from prior test runs appeared alongside my newly submitted task. A first-time user would be confused seeing tasks they didn't create.
sections.label: Actual Behavior

sections.body: Agent tasks are persisted to a shared task store on disk (likely in the Browser4 backend's data directory). There is no session-scoping or automatic expiry — tasks accumulate across CLI sessions until explicitly cleared.
sections.label: Root Cause Analysis

sections.body:
- Consider auto-clearing terminal tasks on CLI startup or session close, or scoping the task store to a session identifier
- Alternatively, add a note in the output when pre-existing tasks are shown: "Showing N tasks (M from prior sessions)"
- Document in SKILL.md that tasks persist across sessions and must be manually cleared
sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement

issues.title: agent status outputs raw JSON by default instead of JSON-enveloped format

sections.body: Run `agent status <id>` and observe raw JSON output. Compare with `agent status <id> --json` which produces a JSON-enveloped format with command/status wrapper.
sections.label: Reproduction

sections.body: Either default output should be JSON-enveloped (consistent with other commands), or the documentation should clearly explain the difference between default and --json output.
sections.label: Expected Behavior

sections.body: Default `agent status` outputs bare JSON (`{"id":...,"statusCode":...}`). With `--json`, output is wrapped (`{"command":"agent-status","output":{"raw":{...}},"status":"ok"}`). This inconsistency means a script parsing `agent status` output gets different structures depending on the --json flag.
sections.label: Actual Behavior

sections.body: The agent status command's default output path bypasses the standard JSON envelope that other commands use. The --json flag re-enables the envelope. This appears to be intentional (raw JSON is more ergonomic for human reading) but creates an inconsistency.
sections.label: Root Cause Analysis

sections.body:
- Document this behavior explicitly in both --help output and SKILL.md
- Consider making the envelope the default for machine consistency, with a --raw flag for bare JSON
sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement

sections.label: Actual Behavior

sections.body: The main help and the category filter likely use different ordering logic — possibly alphabetical vs. declaration order in the clap configuration.
sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
